NEW DELHI: The MK Stalin-led Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam on Thursday launched a sharp attack on Tamil Nadu chief minister C Vijay Joseph, accusing him of taking a "U-turn" on the issue of delimitation.The DMK 's criticism came after Vijay met Union home minister Amit Shah in Tamil Nadu on Thursday.Taking to social media, the DMK IT cell alleged that Vijay, who had earlier taken a strong stand against the Centre and Amit Shah over the issue of delimitation, had now changed his position.The party wrote, "Chief minister Vijay, who took a firm stand against Amit Shah on the issue of delimitation. Chief Minister Vijay, who, in the very same week that a resolution was passed to not increase the current number of 543 MPs, changed his stance."In another post, the DMK said, "Chief Minister Vijay has done a U-turn in a week on the constituency redrawing issue! Is this the same person who called Tamil Nadu's supporters of constituency redrawing the 'eight-footers'?"The party also took a veiled jibe at TVK allies in state, "Will the parties in the alliance question the duplicity in this double game by Thavega? Or will they also give a nod to this?"The attack came on a day Amit Shah chaired the 31st meeting of the Southern Zonal Council in Chengalpet, Tamil Nadu, bringing together representatives of five states and three Union territories to discuss issues concerning the Centre and the southern region.The meeting was held at the Taj Fisherman's Cove hotel in Kovalam and was hosted by the Tamil Nadu government. Chief ministers and senior representatives from the member states and Union territories attended the meeting, according to the ministry of home affairs.
Article Summary: Stalin-led party accuses Vijay of taking 'U-turn' after meeting Amit Shah. The DMK IT cell alleged that Vijay, who had earlier taken a strong stand against the Centre and Amit Shah over the issue of delimitation, had now changed his position.

Article Title: 'We fought wars with Pakistan too, but China will be India's main competitor': Ex-Army chief
Article Text:
General MM Naravane (Retd) on China and Pakistan

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Former Army chief General MM Naravane (Retired) on Thursday described China as India's "main competitor" in the years ahead, despite India having fought wars with both China and Pakistan."Pakistan and China are a totally different ballgame. We have fought wars with both of them. We have unsettled borders. So they will always remain on our radar as a threat, as a challenge," PTI quoted Naravane as saying at a book launch event in New Delhi.However, he distinguished between the two, saying India's immediate focus on Pakistan was driven largely by the continuing threat of terrorism, while describing China as a "competitor" rather than an "enemy." He emphasised that he had "purposely" used the term "competitor" for China."We have fought major wars with Pakistan, and because of their continued support to terrorism, our attention is towards our western borders. But I think we are very clear that in the long term and in the years to come, China is going to be our main competitor. And I purposely use the word competitor and not enemy," Naravane said.Naravane, who was Chief of Army Staff during the 2020 Ladakh clashes with China and led India's response, further stated that the two countries would be competitors across multiple domains, including politics, economics, trade and military affairs."They are going to be our main competitor in all fields. Political, economic, trade, and of course military also. And wherever there is competition, there is always a little bit of conflict," the retired Army general observed.He emphasised that India should seek to manage such differences through dialogue and diplomatic mechanisms rather than resorting to force."It is up to us to try to resolve those conflicts, those differences, through the mechanisms of talks, dialogues. And taking recourse to the use of force should always be the last priority," he said.However, he also stressed that India must maintain credible military preparedness to deter any potential misadventure."There comes a moment when you realise that this is not going to happen. And therefore, you have to have a strong deterrence. That is why the armed forces have to be ready at all times. You have to have a strong deterrence to stop anybody from taking recourse to the use of force or any misadventure," he remarked.
Article Summary: Former Army chief describes China as India's "main competitor" despite India having fought wars with both China and Pakistan. He distinguished between the two, saying India's immediate focus on Pakistan was driven largely by the continuing threat of terrorism. He emphasised that he had "purposely" used the term "competitor" for China.

Article Title: Ex-IAF vice-chief Kapoor says India’s 4.5-gen Tejas may not have relevance in 2030s, country must partner with global consortiums like FCAS or GCAP for 6th-gen programme
Article Text:
Air Marshal Kapoor (Retd) did not totally rule out the role of Tejas Mk2 in future

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Less than two months after retirement as the IAF's vice chief, Air Marshal Nagesh Kapoor (Retd) has slammed the delay in the delivery of Tejas (LCA) fighter jet by Hindustan Aeronautics Limited to the air force, saying, “why must it be that a machine that was promised to us so many years back with a certain set of capabilities continues to be denied to us on one pretext or the other”.In an interview to NDTV, the IAF veteran said, “Why must we be hamstrung because someone somewhere has not been able to keep their promises?”The delivery of the indigenous LCA Tejas Mk1A jets by HAL to the IAF has faced multi-year delays, primarily caused by late supplies of F404-IN20 engines by American GE company, complex mission software validation, and stringent operational requirements set by the IAF.When asked if advanced Tejas Mk-2 may be operationally relevant when it starts entering service in big numbers in mid 2030s at a time when China is already raising its fleet of its 5th-generation fighter jet, the former vice-chief said, “No, operationally, definitely no.”With China on its way to deploying 500 5th-generation J-20 fighters by 2030, India is still struggling to get the delivery of the first squadron by 4.5-generation Tejas Mk1A. Though the IAF had placed orders for a total of 180 Tejas Mk1A fighter jets long ago, HAL hopes to deliver the first 18-25 Tejas Mk1A only by March 2027.Air Marshal Kapoor (Retd) did not totally rule out the role of Tejas Mk2 in future when he said, “You can have a certain number of those 5th generation and 6th generation fighters, but given the size of the country, you won't be able to deploy them everywhere.So those gaps which continue to remain to be filled will have to be filled by this class of aircraft.” “I want Tejas Mk-2 to come, I want India’s 5th-gen AMCA to come. But they must come at a much faster speed,” he said.When asked about Russia’s 5th-gen fighter jet Su-57, the former vice-chief said when the Russian fighter is compared to western jets like American F-35, western jets have an edge over the Su-57 as they have better avionics and stealth.Air Marshal Kapoor (Retd) suggested that India should partner with an European consortium working on state-of-the-art sixth generation platforms. “There are other things that are happening — why not join FCAS (Future Combat Air System is the European programme for 6th generation jet under development by French Dassault Aviation, Airbus and Indra Sistemas) Why not GCAP (Global Combat Air Programme is a multinational initiative led by Italy, Japan, and UK to jointly develop a sixth-generation jet).“'You are probably going with a consortium which has got a good record of delivery, of development. Why go through this Gen 4, Gen 4.5 steps when you know the next best thing is already being thought of and why not just join up there?,” the IAF veteran said.His comments underline the difficult choices facing India’s air power planners: meeting immediate squadron requirements while ensuring that indigenous programmes do not fall behind the rapid evolution of military aviation technology.
Article Summary: Air Marshal Nagesh Kapoor (Retd) has slammed the delay in the delivery of Tejas (LCA) fighter jet by Hindustan Aeronautics Limited. The delivery of the indigenous LCA Tejas Mk1A jets by HAL to the IAF has faced multi-year delays.

Article Title: One is not born, but becomes: India's drag story, from myth to modern stage
Article Text:
India has a rich but complex history of men performing femininity—one that modern drag queens are reclaiming with agency, drawing from both Indian tradition and global queer culture

The history of 'drag' in India

Contemporary drag

Drag queen: Lush Monsoon

Drag queen: Noor Sins

The most heavily quoted feminist scholar, Simone de Beauvoir, launched entire fields of feminist theory by writing - one is not born, but rather becomes, a woman.To be a woman, to be feminine was never purely biological, it was also societal. You are shaped into a woman, piece by piece, experience by experience.In her rejection of the arbitrariness one would often attach to what femininity means, she made space for who some would argue is very much a queer icon and a scholar.Almost half a century later, RuPaul said: we’re all born naked, and the rest is drag.It's a strange thing, watching a philosopher and a reality show host arrive at the same conclusion from opposite directions, that gender was never the given, natural thing it pretends to be, just the costume everyone's already wearing. De Beauvoir got there through existentialism. RuPaul got there through sequins. Both arrived to the conclusion that the performance was the point all along.A common practice to define drag would be to trace its historic roots in the Indian subcontinent. Women were kept out of public spaces, be it India or the West. So when women roles had to be filled in theatrical production men would dress us as them and take up that role in the public eye.India has its own unique lineage to give to this art form, be it through mythology or folk dance and other cultural performances. In the Natyashastra, men played goddesses, heroines, demonesses, styled into femininity through gesture, costume, and the trained emotionDance forms like Kathakali, Jatra and Yakshagana still carry that inheritance. These traditions though have never termed themselves as drag and only trace lineage through reductive definitions of drag being men becoming women convincingly enough to make an audience believe it.India's mythology also builds gender transformation directly into the stories being told. In the Mahabharata's Virata Parva, Arjuna spends a year of exile disguised as Brihannala, a court dancer and music teacher, cursed by the nymph Urvashi to live without his manhood after refusing her. Shikhandi was also born a woman, raised as a warrior, and eventually granted manhood by a Yaksha to fulfil a vow of vengeance against Bhishma.None of this stayed confined to myth and stage. In Ahmedabad, on the eighth night of Navratri, men of the Barot community drape themselves in saris and jewellery to dance garba. In Kottankulangara, Kerala, thousands of men dress as women each year for Chamayavilakku, offering prayers to the goddess Durga at a temple local legend says was born from a bleeding stone, with no women present at the founding moment, boys dressed as women to complete the ritual.Outside temple and epic, there is the tradition of Launda Naach, male dancers performing in women's dress at weddings, in the North Indian belt. It's argued to be India's oldest living form of vernacular drag but it shows no interest in being called "drag".India’s modern drag is a celebration of the feminine inside a being, a lot of what we try to say it draws its lineage from was never a celebration. In some instances it was perversion and in most it was erasure of women from public spaces.A man performing femininity is not automatically a drag queen.The historical circumstances matter. Who was performing? Why were they performing? Who was watching? Who was excluded from the performance? And, crucially, who controlled what that performance meant?For Lush Monsoon, who was among the early generation of contemporary drag performers in Delhi, the relationship between these histories and modern drag is complicated by the question of agency.To her the art forms are exploitative, even if they are often posed as a celebration of queer history. She points to the gaze surrounding these traditions, and to the people who historically inhabit this gaze.“I always see them as an extension of that you are afraid of the feminine, so you are more okay with the masculine projecting as a feminine, and you putting their desire on that.”The issue, she says, is not only about the audience.A lot of the participants are queer. They are queer people from marginalised sections of society or spaces where the language of queer is not defined yet somehow exploited.A younger drag queen too, who has been in this space for around one year, held the same belief. They said that India has a culture of gender intermixing, something we can draw out as a rich queer heritage but modern drag is not a direct extension of this.“The reason that I got attracted to this form of drag, because I saw a certain amount of agency in it.”The point is not to deny India’s rich queer history but to make space for its even more vibrant present.As of today, there are only a handful of venues and spaces for drag performers. Most of the queens interviewed said Indian drag still doesn't carry the same stature as its Western counterpart, which makes it hard to find venues, build audiences, and turn performance into a sustainable career.Venues like KittySu and the Lalit chain of hotels pioneered the space, and it's now getting a push from queer collectives like the GaySi family and smaller creators trying to build safer rooms for queens and their audiences.Yet, reaching a wider audience in the digital era will take a digital push. Every queen interviewed named the same first encounter with drag as an art form: RuPaul's Drag Race. The show cemented its place in queer history, but there's a need for an Indian platform that celebrates queerness and the art form on its own terms, instead of reducing it to comedy.Older drag queens have long faced the accusation of importing a Western culture that maligns Indian heritage. But that heritage has always had space for queer stories. It was colonialism that maligned it, criminalising hijra communities and policing gender through an imported Victorian morality, codified in 1861 as Section 377, a law that stayed on the books for 157 years until the Supreme Court struck it down in 2018.Getting there took decades of work the current generation didn't have to do from scratch. Earlier drag queens fought not just for legal recognition but for the art form itself – pulling it apart from the crass, punchline version of drag Indian television has long been comfortable with.Noor Sins, a younger queen, put it simply: that fight mattered because it meant queens her age could grow up with contemporary, Indian, queer icons to look up to, not borrowed ones.It is perhaps here that the history of Indian drag and what Indian drag is becomes more interesting. In some sense drag always existed but for a lot of contemporary queens what did not exist was the ability to see themselves in the person performing it.The queens performing on stage are taking a form that has so often been used to make femininity into spectacle and making spectacle something they control. They are borrowing from the West without necessarily belonging to it, and drawing from Indian history without pretending that every man who ever wore a sari was a drag queen.The world is changing, the queens coming up now get to inherit something their predecessors had to build: a language, a community, spaces to perform, and most importantly, people who look like them already standing on a stage. But the stage has to become bigger, and the language more universal.De Beauvoir never wrote about drag. But she wrote the sentence that explains why it matters: one is not born, but becomes. For the queens performing in India today, that becoming is not simply about becoming a woman through makeup and dresses. It is about becoming visible to themselves, and then to one another, in a form that did not always give them someone to see.
Article Summary: India has its own unique lineage to give to this art form, be it through mythology or folk dance and other cultural performances. In the Natyashastra, men played goddesses, heroines, demonesses, styled into femininity through gesture, costume, and the trained emotion. A man performing femininity is not automatically a drag queen.

Article Title: Invoking Mahatma Gandhi, BJP to start nationwide Vande campaign
Article Text:
The campaign was approved at a meet of new office-bearers Saturday

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Month-long campaign for PM Modi's birthday

NEW DELHI: BJP cited Mahatma Gandhi's "we have fallen on evil days" lament over the opposition built up against Vande Mataram Saturday to set the stage for an intense political battle with Congress and the wider 'secular' class for their objections to the national song's full version by announcing a nationwide campaign.The campaign, approved at a meeting of the new office-bearers under party chief Nitin Nabin, will focus on the song's association with freedom struggle, opposition by Pakistan's founder M A Jinnah and other Muslim hardliners which led Congress to prune it and "communal pressure or narrow vote-bank considerations" driving the current protests against the national song.The meeting adopted a four-page resolution, accusing Congress of "bowing before the same politics of appeasement" to which it had yielded in 1937, enabling Jinnah-led Muslim League to impose communal demands even upon national symbols.BJP's decision to launch the 10-point campaign comes after Congress asserted that it will stick to its 1937 resolution that had adopted the first two stanzas of Vande Mataram to signal its defiance of the notification restoring its full version for all official events and Parliament passing a law making any insult to the song a penal offence. With Gen Z emerging as an axis of political mobilisation for its rivals after their successful protest over paper leaks, the campaign also seeks to target its pitch for Vande Mataram at the youth.PM Modi visited party headquarters to interact with the new team. Organisational meetings are all about new ideas aimed at strengthening the party and deepening connection with the people, he said.In its resolution, BJP marshalled comments of stalwarts like Gandhi and C Rajagopalachari to hit back at its rivals, who have accused it of stoking political divide over the song. It framed its campaign as a contest between the song's rich legacy versus a bid to truncate it to appease Muslim fundamentalists.It cited Gandhi's 1939 comments: "I associated the purest national spirit with it (Vande Mataram). It never occurred to me that it was a Hindu song or meant only for Hindus. Unfortunately, now we have fallen on evil days." Nabin accused Congress of sowing the same seeds of division that it did in 1937 by adopting a truncated version under the Muslim League's pressure.Several youth-centric programmes will be part of BJP's month-long campaign from Modi's birthday on Sept 17, with the annual "sewa" programme turning special this time as he will also be completing 25 years as head of a govt.
Article Summary: Campaign will focus on song's association with freedom struggle, opposition by Pakistan's founder M A Jinnah and other Muslim hardliners. Meeting adopted a four-page resolution accusing Congress of "bowing before the same politics of appeasement" to which it had yielded in 1937.

Article Title: Caitlin Clark’s emotional Kobe Bryant connection resurfaces as her own Nike shoe prepares to launch
Article Text:
USA Basketball makes long awaited Caitlin Clark decision as Women’s World Cup roster finally settles Olympic debate

Caitlin Clark’s Kobe Bryant sneaker connection started in high school

Caitlin Clark wants fans to feel connected to her Nike shoe

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Caitlin Clark’s connection to Kobe Bryant goes beyond basketball. Long before she became one of the WNBA’s biggest stars and prepared to launch her own Nike signature shoe, Clark was simply a young basketball fan who loved sneakers. Her memories of customizing Kobe shoes now carry a different meaning as she prepares to give fans a chance to experience that same personal connection through the Caitlin 1.Clark has openly embraced sneaker culture throughout her rise in basketball. Before the attention, endorsements and signature footwear, she was a teenager looking for ways to make her favorite shoes feel more personal.That included Nike iD, the customization platform now known as Nike By You. For Clark, customizing Kobe Bryant sneakers offered more than a chance to change colors or add personal touches. It allowed her to feel connected to a player she admired.“As somebody who’s been a sneakerhead her whole life and has always wanted the newest pair of shoes, even when I was in high school, I remember going on Nike iD and iDing my own Kobes,” Clark said.The memory stands out because it captures a side of Clark that existed before she became a household name.She was not wearing a signature shoe of her own. She was a fan, choosing details for shoes linked to one of basketball’s most influential stars.That makes her story particularly fitting now. Clark is preparing to step into the same world that once fascinated her from the outside.The Caitlin 1 is scheduled to become available worldwide on October 1, giving Clark an opportunity to turn her own sneaker philosophy into something fans can share.Her goal appears to be bigger than simply putting her name on a shoe. Clark remembers what it felt like to customize footwear connected to a favorite player, and she wants her supporters to experience a similar sense of ownership.“I always loved getting to do that and making it your own, but at the same time, it’s still your favourite player’s and you’re kind of sharing that with them.“So, I hope when people grab the bright blue box, I hope you feel it right when you grab the box off the shelf, that it’s pure joy and fire and passion and it’s a part of me.”That final thought explains why the Kobe connection matters. Bryant’s shoes once gave Clark a way to express her admiration while making the footwear feel like her own. Now, Clark is on the other side of that relationship.Fans will soon be able to buy a shoe carrying her identity, style and basketball journey. For Clark, that creates a full-circle moment. The young sneakerhead who once customized Kobes is now creating a signature shoe that she hopes another generation will customize, wear and remember.The Caitlin 1 therefore represents more than another athlete-branded release. It reflects how basketball culture passes from one generation to the next, with inspiration changing hands while the passion remains.
Article Summary: Caitlin Clark's Kobe Bryant sneaker connection started in high school. The Caitlin 1 is scheduled to become available worldwide on October 1. It reflects how basketball culture passes from one generation to the next. Clark wants her supporters to experience a similar sense of ownership.

Article Title: "Erika and TPUSA are watching every single one of her shows": Candace Owens could face costly legal battle as Erika Kirk and Turning Point USA reportedly prepare for potential lawsuit
Article Text:
Candace Owens and Erika Kirk (Image via Getty Images)

Myron Gaines predicts Erika Kirk and TPUSA could build a case against Candace Owens

Candace Owens lawsuit prediction hinges on a higher defamation standard

A fresh wave of legal speculation is building around Candace Owens after Myron Gaines predicted that Erika Kirk and Turning Point USA could eventually pursue a costly defamation case against the conservative commentator. Gaines did not claim a lawsuit has been filed. Instead, he argued that Owens’ broadcasts may be closely documented and preserved for possible legal action after the Tyler Robinson criminal case reaches a decisive point.The claim gained attention after a social media post suggested a “Candace Owens lawsuit” could be coming. The important distinction is that Gaines presented the scenario as his own prediction, not as confirmation from Erika Kirk, TPUSA, their attorneys, or a court filing.His argument centers on timing. Gaines believes any potential legal action would be stronger after Tyler Robinson’s case is resolved and more evidence has emerged publicly. He also suggested that Owens’ past and future broadcasts could become important if a defamation dispute ever reaches court.Gaines said:“What I anticipate is this. Erika Kirk and Turning Point USA are gonna wait until Tyler Robinson is convicted.Once Tyler Robinson is convicted and more evidence comes out during a trial, I think that's when they're gonna hit Candace with the lawsuits.Best believe that fucking Erika Kirk and Turning Point USA are watching every single one of her shows, saving the videos, saving every single clip that they think is gonna be considered defamation, and they're building a case right now as we speak. I guarantee you guys. They're watching every single broadcast, anytime she insinuates that Erika Kirk was involved in a murder, or that Turning Point USA was covering it up, or anything, or when she made the comment that like, oh, you guys shouldn't donate any money to Turning Point, they're corrupt, they're going to document all of that shit, dude.They probably already have every single clip right now saved somewhere. After the trial happens, and if Tyler Robinson is found guilty, they're gonna serve her with a lawsuit. That's what I think they're angling to do right now.And I think Erika Kirk only met with Candace Owens on earlier this, late last year, I think it was. I think they met either early this year or late last year. I think she literally only met her just to check a box and say, I met with her, I tried to tell her what it was, and she's still attacking me.Because you guys got to understand, from a legal strategic perspective, that as a public figure, it is really hard for you to prove defamation. Because as a public figure, you don't have some of the same benefits that private citizens are able to enjoy when you're a private citizen. Or sorry, when you're a public figure, excuse me.”Gaines then turned to the legal challenge that would accompany such a case. In the United States, public figures generally face a demanding standard in defamation litigation. They may need to establish “actual malice,” which concerns whether a defamatory statement was made with knowledge that it was false or with reckless disregard for whether it was true.That does not mean Gaines’ interpretation establishes that Owens has committed defamation, nor does it prove that Erika Kirk or TPUSA intends to sue her. Those questions would depend on the specific statements involved, the evidence, applicable law and, ultimately, the courts.Gaines continued:“So the threshold for defamation when you're a public figure is significantly higher, because now you have to establish defamation with malice. So if Erika Kirk and TPUSA were to sue Candace, they would have to prove that she not only defamed Erika Kirk, but she defamed Erika Kirk with malicious intent, and she knowingly did it, contrary to knowing the truth. So that's what they're gonna have to prove.What I predict is, is they're going to build their case, wait till Tyler Robinson is convicted, wait until she says, I still think he's a patsy, and then they're gonna hit her with the fucking they're gonna hit her with the lawsuit. I like Candace, you guys know this, I get along with her. But I do think that a very expensive lawsuit is coming her way very soon from TPUSA.And then they got the money to do it, bro. An organization like that has like millions upon millions of dollars in their war chest for shit like this. And you don't think those Jewish donors will put money in to get the best lawyers to go after her? What do you think?And then not only are they going to go after Candace, because she's the, you know, the most famous, etc.She also has money. I'm sure she's making anywhere from 500,000 to a million dollars a month right now. I have no doubt in my mind she's making that kind of money right now.And then Turning Point is going to use that to say, look, look how much money she's made off of us. You got to prove damages too. They're going to say, we estimate she made, you know, 15 million dollars, because they're probably gonna have forensic accountants on their shit too.Guaranteed. And they're gonna absolutely go after her and try to collect as much money as they can. But Candace is smart.I'm sure she already has money set aside for lawsuits like this. But yeah, that's my prediction.”The final words are crucial to understanding the story: Gaines repeatedly characterized the scenario as a prediction. His comments about TPUSA’s finances, Owens’ income, potential damages and the motives or actions of donors were also his own assertions and estimates, not established facts presented in the supplied material.For now, the significance of the clip lies in the possibility Gaines raised rather than an announced legal battle. Unless Erika Kirk, Turning Point USA or their representatives confirm legal action, talk of an impending lawsuit against Candace Owens remains speculation rather than a filed case.
Article Summary: Myron Gaines predicts Erika Kirk and TPUSA could build a case against Candace Owens. Gaines did not claim a lawsuit has been filed. Instead, he argued that Owens’ broadcasts may be closely documented and preserved for possible legal action after the Tyler Robinson case reaches a decisive point.

Article Title: Inspiring story on motherhood: “It’s not easy. It’s been one of the most challenging things in my life” - How Erin Andrews turned years of fertility struggles into a powerful message of hope
Article Text:
Erin Andrews (Image via Imagn Images)

Erin Andrews opens up about her difficult fertility journey

Why Erin Andrews refused to hide her IVF struggles

Seinfeld

Erin Andrews and Jarret Stoll eventually welcomed their son

Erin Andrews’ motherhood story continues beyond Mack

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Erin Andrews spent years reporting from some of the biggest sporting events in America, but one of the hardest battles of her life happened far away from the cameras. Her journey toward motherhood involved years of fertility treatment, emotional setbacks and difficult choices. Instead of keeping that pain private, Andrews chose to speak openly about it, hoping her experience could make another woman feel less alone.Long before Erin Andrews became a mother, she had already spent years navigating the uncertainty of trying to build a family.In January 2023, the sportscaster spoke candidly with Us Weekly about the emotional weight of IVF and the effect it had on both her and her husband, former NHL player Jarret Stoll. She did not pretend the experience was easy.“It’s not easy. It’s been one of the most challenging things in my life, and I know in my husband’s life as well,” Andrews told Us Weekly. “I’m doing OK. We’re doing well.”Those words captured the reality of a journey that had already lasted for years.Andrews had previously revealed in a 2021 essay for Bulletin that she had been undergoing fertility treatments since she was 35.She described the process as emotionally draining and explained how isolating infertility could feel when people rarely talked openly about it.Her decision to speak publicly was not simply about telling her own story. Andrews wanted to challenge the shame that can surround fertility struggles.She explained to Us Weekly that Stoll had initially questioned why she was so open about their experience. But once Andrews began talking, she discovered just how many other people were facing similar challenges. She said she hoped conversations like those could eventually lead to support groups or foundations for people dealing with infertility.Her central message was simple: infertility should not be something people feel ashamed to discuss.The physical side of IVF became another part of Andrews’ story.With her characteristic humor, she joked about handling repeated injections better than her husband. She told Us Weekly that she could take roughly 50 needles in her stomach and keep going, while Stoll would retreat to another room and watchBehind the joke was something more serious. Andrews had discovered a strength in herself that she did not know she possessed.“You know that you’re strong and that you can deal with it and it will get better,” she said.That attitude became an important part of how she approached the uncertainty.Andrews also said humor helped her cope. Rather than pretending every day was positive, she found value in being honest with close friends. Sometimes, she explained, she could simply acknowledge that the situation was awful. On other days, she could celebrate encouraging news.That honesty made her story relatable. Fertility struggles do not follow a neat emotional script. There can be hope one day and disappointment the next.For Andrews, acknowledging both sides became part of surviving the experience.Months after Andrews spoke about her fertility struggles, her story took a life-changing turn.In July 2023, Andrews and Stoll welcomed their first child, a son named Mack, via surrogate after years of fertility challenges. The arrival marked a major moment for the couple and brought a new dimension to Andrews’ long journey toward motherhood.The birth itself was not entirely without fear.Andrews later revealed that there had been a brief emergency in the delivery room after the surrogate dilated rapidly and concerns arose about the baby’s heartbeat. The moment passed quickly, and Andrews recalled that the surrogate pushed once before Mack arrived.The memory stayed with Andrews because of what it represented. After years of treatments, setbacks and uncertainty, she was finally watching her son enter the world.She later described a photograph from that moment as a perfect picture of surrogacy. In it, Andrews was kissing the surrogate’s head while Stoll looked overwhelmed with emotion.Motherhood did not erase the complicated emotions attached to Andrews’ fertility journey.In 2024, she acknowledged that she and Stoll were considering trying for another child. But she also admitted that the thought of returning to fertility treatment frightened her because she did not want to experience another period of failure after the joy surrounding Mack’s birth.That vulnerability is what makes Andrews’ story particularly powerful.Her experience shows that becoming a parent after infertility does not necessarily erase the memories of what came before. The fear can remain. So can the emotional scars.In 2025, Andrews also revealed that a surrogate had suffered a miscarriage during another attempt to expand their family. She spoke about the heartbreak with the same openness that had defined her earlier fertility discussions.Through it all, Andrews has continued to make one point clear: people should not have to suffer in silence.Her story is not simply about IVF, surrogacy or becoming a mother. It is about resilience and the courage to admit when something hurts.Years after she first described fertility treatment as one of the hardest experiences of her life, Andrews’ openness has given another generation of hopeful parents something valuable: permission to talk about the difficult parts.And perhaps that is the most meaningful part of her motherhood story. She did not wait until everything was perfect to speak. She opened up while she was still figuring it out, proving that sometimes the most powerful stories are the ones told before the ending is known.
Article Summary: Erin Andrews and Jarret Stoll welcomed their first child, a son named Mack, via surrogate in July 2023. Andrews had previously revealed in a 2021 essay that she had been undergoing fertility treatments since she was 35. In 2024, Andrews acknowledged that she and Stoll were considering trying for another child.

Simone Biles has never been shy about sharing the lighter, more unexpected moments of her life with fans. But one social media interaction left the Olympic champion genuinely puzzled. The seven-time Olympic gold medalist recently recalled an awkward exchange with an unnamed influencer after she reached out for a hairstylist recommendation. What began as a simple beauty question quickly became an interaction Biles still finds strange enough to remember years later.Biles said she had followed the influencer for some time because she admired her fashion, content and, especially, her consistently polished hair. At the time, Biles was also paying close attention to her own hair after facing repeated criticism over her appearance during gymnastics competitions.Her curiosity eventually led her to send a direct message asking about the stylist behind the influencer's looks. The answer, however, was not what Biles expected."The reason why I followed her is because I loved her style, her content," Biles said. "She was super, super cute, but her hair was always laid to a T.Like, I could not tell if that was her real hair or a weave. And at the time, I was like …I would say, particular about hair."Biles explained why the question mattered to her at the time."I didn't really give a f*** that much, but, like, y'all have been bullying me for so long about what my hair looked like during competitions so I'm like, 'OK, if my hair looks like that, they're not gonna say anything.'"The response from the influencer, though, caught Biles off guard."She replies, 'Bless. My manager has it. I'll have to ask her,'" Biles said, slamming her tablet closed. "What? You don't know who does your hair when you go to your hair appointments? You don't have their contact or Instagram? Like, I get gatekeeping, but to a certain extent."Rather than seeing the request as a possible attempt to take the stylist, Biles said she simply wanted another option available when traveling. She also pointed out that she and the influencer lived in different states, making the idea of directly competing for the same hairstylist seem unlikely.Biles eventually unfollowed the influencer, but the encounter apparently stayed with her. She admitted that she continues to think about the exchange and remains unsure whether she was overreacting or whether the response was genuinely unusual."And mind you, we lived in two different states, so I think maybe she thought, like, I was gonna steal her hairstylist or something, but that's not at all what it was. I travel all the time, so if I'm ever in that area, like, 'Hey, let me get slayed real quick.'"Biles later put the entire situation to her followers, turning an uncomfortable memory into a funny social media moment."But isn't that weird? Is that weird or that's just me?" she asked. "Does that happen to y'all? I don't know. I just. To this day, I still think about it, and it cracks me up, but also, like, what? Yeah. I don't know."The gymnast has also shown that she is perfectly comfortable reaching out to celebrities herself. At a July appearance at the Faces of Fitness festival in Chicago, Biles shared another amusing social media story involving singer Avril Lavigne. After Lavigne apparently ended up with her YSL sunglasses, Biles said she sent a direct message asking, "Yo, can I get those YSLs back?"Lavigne had not responded at the time Biles shared the story. Together, the anecdotes offer a glimpse of Biles away from competition: direct, playful and willing to laugh about the odd encounters that follow life in the public eye.

Article Title: "She didn't feel like I was doing my part": Tom Brady revealed the heartbreaking moment Gisele Bündchen told him she was no longer happy in their marriage

Why Gisele Bündchen felt alone in the marriage

What Tom Brady did to save his marriage

Some confessions don't come from a press conference podium. They come from a radio studio, when a guy famous for keeping his personal life locked away finally decides to unlock it. That's exactly what happened when Tom Brady sat down with Howard Stern in 2020 and admitted his marriage to Gisele Bündchen had quietly started cracking under the weight of his football career.The problem wasn't a single fight or one bad season. It built up over years. Brady spent every fall and winter buried in football, and the moment the season wrapped, he didn't slow down. He jumped straight into training and business ventures, leaving Bündchen to manage the house, the kids, and everything in between, largely on her own.Brady laid it out plainly to Stern. "A couple of years ago, she didn't feel like I was doing my part for the family," he said. "She felt like I would play football all season and she would take care of the house, and then all of a sudden when the season would end, I'd be like, 'Great, let me get into all of my other business activities. Let me get into my football training,' and she's sitting there going, 'Well, when are you going to do things for the house? When are you going to take the kids to school and do that?'"It wasn't just about chores or scheduling. Bündchen was asking for something bigger, and Brady knew it."And that was a big part of our marriage," he continued. "I had to, like, check myself. Because she's like, 'I have goals and dreams too. It's not just doing this and this. You better start taking care of things at the house.'"Hearing one of the most decorated athletes in sports history admit he needed to "check himself" said more about his marriage than any highlight reel ever could.Talk is easy. Brady backed his words with action. He stepped away from the Patriots' voluntary offseason program, a decision most players in his position would never make, so he could actually be present at home. The couple also started counseling together, working through frustration that had clearly been sitting under the surface for a while.One detail from that chapter has stuck with Brady long after the arguments faded. Bündchen wrote him a letter putting her feelings into words, and he still keeps it close. "She actually wrote me a letter, and it was a very thought-out letter that she wrote to me and I still have it and I keep it in a drawer and I read it," he shared."It's a very heartfelt letter for her to say this is where I'm at in our marriage, and it's a good reminder for me that things are going to change and evolve over time. What happened and what worked for us 10 years ago won't work for us forever, because we are growing in different ways."That last line is the real takeaway. Marriages don't run on autopilot, even for people who seem to have everything figured out. Brady's honesty about that struggle turned a private low point into a reminder that even a Super Bowl winner has to keep showing up, at home and not just on the field.
Article Summary: Tom Brady's marriage to Gisele Bündchen had quietly started cracking under the weight of his football career. Brady spent every fall and winter buried in football, and the moment the season wrapped, he didn't slow down. He stepped away from the Patriots' voluntary offseason program so he could actually be present at home.

Article Title: Chiefs players reportedly turn on Travis Kelce in private group chats as controversial decisions spark locker-room drama

Travis Kelce’s wedding to Taylor Swift may have brought together two of the biggest names in sports and entertainment, but the guest list is now drawing attention for a very different reason. Reports of Chiefs players discussing the invitations in private group chats have added an unexpected layer of locker-room intrigue, with Harrison Butker’s absence reportedly becoming one of the main talking points ahead of training camp.The wedding reportedly drew more than 1,000 guests, including family members, close friends and several prominent Kansas City Chiefs figures. Patrick and Brittany Mahomes, Andy Reid, Chris Jones and Isiah Pacheco were among the football names reported to have attended.But not everyone connected to the Chiefs received the same treatment. According to the report cited by The Red Zone, some players discussed the guest list and Butker’s absence in private conversations.One unnamed Chiefs player reportedly explained that the situation was less hostile than some social media reactions suggested, while acknowledging that teammates had plenty to say behind the scenes."It’s really their wedding, and I understand why they wouldn’t have invited [Butker]. But there’s some difference of opinion [between players]. Lots of texts are going around the team, and some people who are close to Harrison feel like he was snubbed.""The general idea was that there was a blanket invite for the team, but [every other player] received something individually. If Harrison had really wanted to come, he probably could have. But they’re not close, so… he wasn’t going to go, even if he had been invited."The same player also described a locker room that enjoys teasing and gossip as much as any other workplace."There’s now a lot of gossip going on. Training camp [for the new NFL season] starts in three weeks, and it’s going to be a whole thing. A lot of guys want it to be drama [between Butker and Kelce]. They just like that s**t… a couple of the guys are being messy and texting Harrison to see what he thinks. We’re like a high school team sometimes."The report also offered a glimpse into how Chiefs players communicate away from the field. Rather than one massive team conversation, players reportedly belong to smaller groups based on friendships, positions and personal relationships.A second unnamed Chiefs player said:‘It’s not like all of us are in the same [group chat]. The team is too big. So there are groups that might just be like defense [players], or a certain group of guys. There are some with me in, some without me. I am in about seven chains of players, some are professional… some are just used for talking s**t.‘I have chains that have Travis on them, and chains that don’t. You always have to check to make sure you’re sending to the right chain. There have been times where you’ll talk s**t about someone and then realize they are in the group, and have to laugh it off.‘I think most of the texts about the wedding are probably being sent in the groups without Travis. I have one that has about eight of us, and, before the wedding, it was like “Who’s going?” And everyone was saying where they were staying, or why they weren’t going.‘I think maybe half the team went, probably less. A lot of people RSVP’d no, not because of anything bad, but because of a conflict. I didn’t go because I didn’t want to spend the 4th in New York and couldn’t bring my kids.‘Some people asked, “Do we have to send them a gift?’, because they have more money than us, which was funny. People were coming up with funny things to send. I thought it would be funny to send him something that was monogrammed “Mr and Mrs Swift”. That type of thing. We sent each other memes and pictures.’The first player later offered another explanation for why the situation should not be viewed as a serious fracture inside the Chiefs.‘Can’t say too much because Travis is my friend… Yeah, there are a few group texts. I’m on one with Harrison [Butker]. Someone sent a news story about him not being invited, and the group was like “WTF?” But he didn’t reply.‘I don’t think anyone on the team wishes [Kelce] anything but good things. Everyone likes him. He’s a good teammate and a good friend. There’s locker room s**t, but it’s nothing disrespectful.‘Most of [our group] texts were just logistics about how people were getting from their hotels to the wedding, or what everyone was going to wear. The women [players’ wives and girlfriends] have other text groups. Taylor is officially a football wife now, and she’ll be invited to their wine nights and stuff, but she won’t go. I’m sure of that. But if you want trash talk, you have to see their group texts. My girlfriend won’t even let me look at her phone to see it. ’For now, the reported wedding chatter appears to be more about teasing, curiosity and differing opinions than a genuine Chiefs feud. Still, with training camp approaching, even small personal stories can attract outsized attention when they involve Kelce, Swift and one of the NFL’s most closely followed locker rooms.

Reports of Chiefs players discussing the invitations in private group chats have added an unexpected layer of locker-room intrigue.

Mumbai: Prabath Jayasuriya is a rarity in modern-day cricket, especially in the subcontinent, where if you are aged 30 and above, you are not favoured to play international cricket. He waited in the shadows of Sri Lanka’s rich spin tradition. When his chance finally arrived in July 2022, the left-arm spinner grabbed it spectacularly, claiming 12 wickets on Test debut against Australia in Galle.Since then, Jayasuriya has carried Sri Lanka’s spin legacy with distinction, taking 132 wickets in 24 Tests. Ahead of the second Test against India at the SSC, the 34-year-old spoke to TOI about his journey, Sri Lanka’s chances of levelling the series, and why he believes India’s young left-arm spinner Manav Suthar can become one of the world’s best. Excerpts...I had waited a long time for that opportunity. I made my debut after turning 30 and it was a dream start. It remains my favourite match in cricket. After that performance, I realised there was a bigger responsibility because I was representing Sri Lanka. Expectations increased and sometimes the team looks to you for something extra.That brings extra pressure.We knew the pitch would be good for batting early on. KL Rahul and Devdutt Padikkal used those conditions very well and built the foundation for India. We improved in the second innings but by then the game had gone away from us. India’s batters handled spin well.India batted really well. As a bowling unit, we need to have clearer plans and also execute them better. If we can do that consistently, I believe we can get a better result in the second Test.Joe Root, Kane Williamson and Steve Smith.As players, we have to believe. We have some challenging series coming up, including away tours of Pakistan and New Zealand and a home series against South Africa. The important thing is to stay focused on our processes.Both Kusal Mendis and Dinesh Chandimal are out...It’s a big loss. Both are experienced players and important members of the team. At the same time, it opens the door for younger players to step in and prove themselves.He has the potential to become one of the best bowlers in the world. He needs to stay committed to the process, work hard and make sacrifices. If he remains consistent, I believe he can achieve great things.The pitch generally starts turning after the first couple of days. Consistency is the key there. If you keep bowling the right line and length, you can be successful. That’s exactly what Manav did in the first Test.The SSC is my home ground because I play my domestic cricket there. I understand the conditions well. The key is to adapt quickly and keep things simple.Every Test batter is a challenge. Devdutt Padikkal played extremely well in Galle and handled both spin and pace impressively. As the lead spinner in the team, I have a big responsibility. Against strong teams, we need detailed plans and extra effort.

Article Title: Is Auston Matthews’ $53 million deal justified after Sid Seixeiro questions the Toronto Maple Leafs captain’s recent production?

Is Auston Matthews overpaid by the Toronto Maple Leafs?

Can Auston Matthews change the conversation in 2026-27?

The Auston Matthews conversation has shifted from his video game rating to a more general discussion of value, production and expectations. The Toronto Maple Leafs captain carries an annual average value of $13.25 million, and his game is a huge part of Toronto’s ability to build a competitive roster.Sid Seixeiro has stated that Matthews' numbers over the last two seasons haven't quite warranted that level of compensation. Complicating the assessment, meanwhile, is the fact that Matthews has missed significant time before undergoing knee surgery after an injury in March. Since then, he’s back on the ice in Arizona, training in advance of the 2026-27 NHL season.The question is; does Auston Matthews’ recent production warrant the $53 million Toronto Maple Leafs contract? Sid Seixeiro says the numbers don’t add up for the price tag right now.Seixeiro's comments came following the release of the EA Sports NHL 27 player ratings, with Matthews rated a 92 overall. That rating has the Toronto Maple Leafs captain out of the game’s top 10 centers, with Connor McDavid leading the position at 99 overall.The rating itself is not a reflection of a player’s real-world value, but Seixeiro used it as a jumping-off point to question whether Matthews is still one of the NHL’s best centers.His argument largely centers on Matthews’ recent statistical production and the expectations that come with one of the league’s largest contracts.Matthews' current contract is for four years and $53 million, with an average annual value of $13.25 million. It also has a no-movement clause, showing the Toronto Maple Leafs are committed to their captain.Matthews finished the 2025-26 NHL season with 27 goals in 60 games, a career-low in terms of goals, and he’s been injury-plagued the last two seasons, so his availability has been a concern too.That context is important when assessing his output, and Matthews has already proven to be one of the best goal scorers in the NHL. It is highlighted by a 69-goal season in 2023-24. His recent decline, then, is a big departure from the standard. That he set earlier in his Toronto Maple Leafs career.If Auston Matthews is healthy, he can quickly change the conversation about his contract, and the 29-year-old center is skating again after having knee surgery and recently participated in the Sun Devil Hockey Pro Camp in Arizona. The return to the ice is a positive development. But it alone doesn't guarantee a full recovery before training camp.The NHL Outlook for the Toronto Maple Leafs in 2026-27: Matthews’ health and scoring touch will be key. If he could return to his previous offensive levels, it would help make the case that his contract is still justified. Another injury-riddled or low-production season could only fuel questions about the deal.The NHL 27 grade is a snapshot of how Matthews is viewed as he enters the new season. The more meaningful test, however, will come when the Toronto Maple Leafs start playing NHL games, and Matthews gets a chance to respond on the ice.

The timeless lesson

The fear of death has troubled humanity for centuries, but Socrates believed there was another danger that deserved far greater concern, compromising one's principles. In Plato's, Socrates argues that “the difficulty, my friends, is not in avoiding death, but in avoiding unrighteousness.” The remark came during his trial in Athens, when he faced the possibility of execution. Rather than treating death as the greatest evil, Socrates placed greater importance on avoiding injustice and wrongdoing. His words suggest that preserving one's moral character can matter more than protecting one's life or reputation. More than two thousand years later, the idea remains relevant in a world where people often face difficult choices between doing what is right and doing what is convenient.Socrates was drawing a distinction between physical survival and moral integrity. Avoiding death may appear to be the most obvious instinct, but he believed that fear of death should not lead a person into wrongdoing. In his view, death is something whose nature humans cannot fully know, while injustice is something a person can recognise through reason and moral judgement. His argument therefore shifts the focus away from the fear of losing one's life and towards the danger of losing one's principles.Socrates suggests that a person should be more concerned about becoming unjust than about suffering an unjust fate. The quote reflects his broader belief that a good life depends not simply on remaining alive, but on living according to virtue and conscience.Human beings naturally try to protect themselves when faced with danger. Yet Socrates questioned whether survival should always be the highest priority. There are situations in which protecting oneself may require lying, betraying someone or acting against one's principles. Socrates' philosophy suggests that such choices can carry a deeper cost than physical danger because they can damage the character of the person making them. His argument therefore presents morality as something that should not be abandoned simply because circumstances become difficult. The lesson is not that life has little value, but that survival at the expense of one's principles may come with a price that is difficult to recover from.Socrates' words can be applied to many of the moral compromises people encounter in everyday life. A person may remain silent when they know something is wrong because speaking up could threaten their career. Someone may participate in dishonest behaviour because refusing could make them unpopular or cost them an opportunity. In public life, politics, business and even personal relationships, people can sometimes face pressure to choose convenience over principle. The quote offers a different way of looking at such situations. It asks whether avoiding immediate consequences is worth compromising the values that define who we are.Socrates made this argument while defending himself against accusations in Athens. He refused to abandon his philosophical mission simply because continuing it had become dangerous. According to Plato's account in Apology, Socrates maintained that he should continue examining himself and others, even if doing so made him unpopular or placed him at risk. His eventual death became one of the most enduring examples in Western philosophy of a person refusing to surrender his principles out of fear. Whether one agrees with every aspect of his philosophy or not, his willingness to accept the consequences of his convictions explains why his words have remained influential for more than two millennia.Socrates' words ultimately offer a powerful reminder that the greatest danger is not always what can happen to us, but what we can become because of what happens to us. Fear, pressure and self-interest can tempt people to abandon principles that once seemed important. Yet Socrates believed that protecting one's moral character was more important than simply avoiding hardship or death. His question therefore remains remarkably contemporary: when circumstances force us to choose between safety and integrity, what are we willing to sacrifice? The answer, according to Socrates, should never be our sense of what is right.
Article Summary: Socrates argued that a person should be more concerned about becoming unjust than about suffering an unjust fate. The quote reflects his broader belief that a good life depends not simply on remaining alive, but on living according to virtue and conscience. His eventual death became one of the most enduring examples in Western philosophy of a person refusing to surrender his principles.

Article Title: ‘Crushed his lungs, calculated conspiracy’: How a ‘minor’ dispute ended in Adobe techie's death
Article Text:

'It was just a minor matter'

'Crushed his lungs'

'Calculated conspiracy'

4 detained





NEW DELHI: ‘It’s a calculated conspiracy’, ‘they crushed his lungs’, said the family of a 31-year-old software engineer who was allegedly beaten to death by his wife’s relatives in Delhi, claiming that the attack was a pre-planned attempt to kill him.Vinay Gupta, who worked at Adobe, was allegedly assaulted at his home in Laxmi Park, Nihal Vihar, on Friday following a matrimonial dispute.Police have detained four people in connection with the case.Gupta's father, Premchand, said the dispute was minor and that he initially believed the relatives had come to discuss the matter."It was just a minor domestic matter. There was nothing major about it. They arrived, and I thought, 'Relatives have come; we'll talk.' I took them upstairs. I was offering them water and such.""Then my son arrived. As soon as he did, they all pounced on him... It happened right in front of me. They even shoved me. I have a fracture in my thumb... They got married three and a half years ago and had two children."Gupta's mother, Renu, alleged that his wife's family attacked him soon after arriving at the house."There was some minor ongoing dispute that I wasn't even aware of.I don't know why she left early in the morning, leaving the two children behind, to go fetch her brothers.""My husband came in and said that the relatives have arrived. I tried to offer them water, but they said, 'We don't want your water.' They immediately grabbed my son.""My husband kept saying, 'Don't raise your hand. Let's talk calmly.' But the older brother, and that stout younger brother of hers, attacked.""The older brother grabbed my son by the hair and threatened to rip it all out. I kept trying to pull him away, but that huge, burly man shoved me aside and threw me down.""He squeezed my son's throat with all his might and then slammed him onto the ground.""A neighbor even witnessed it from the window, seeing both brothers stomping on my son's chest, crushing his lungs...""I grabbed a stick to defend him, but it was snatched away by an uncle who had come with them. They beat my son and left."Gupta's mother also alleged that the security cameras were not working at the time of the assault."The security cameras happened to be turned off at that exact moment. I don't know if it was the daughter-in-law's plan or if they had plotted it beforehand. I can't say for sure.""We had absolutely no intention of getting into a fight. Minor domestic squabbles happen all the time, but they came there with a calculated, sinister plan. They came with the intent to kill my son."Gupta's brother, Pradeep, said he reached the spot after the assault and found his brother in a critical condition."When I went there, I saw that after the scuffle, the young man was lying there in a critical condition. If he had been taken to the hospital half an hour earlier, he might have survived.""I can't even comprehend the nature of the beating. Only a cunning, malicious person could understand it. We might slap someone on the cheek or hit them on the leg, but the way they hit him.""He passed away on the way... The girl's father, her two brothers, her sister-in-law, and the girl herself were all involved...""I know the young man well. He never spoke rudely to anyone. It seems like a calculated conspiracy. The assault was so brutal."Police said the dispute between Gupta and his wife began on Friday morning. His wife allegedly called her family, who then reached Gupta's residence in Nihal Vihar and allegedly assaulted him.Gupta suffered serious injuries and later succumbed to them. Police said four people allegedly involved in the attack have been identified and detained.A case under Sections 103(1), relating to murder, and 3(5), relating to common intention, of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) is being registered.Gupta had married the 31-year-old woman from Budh Vihar about three-and-a-half years ago.The couple have four-month-old twins, a boy and a girl. His wife is a homemaker.The detained people are being questioned about their alleged roles in the assault. Police are also probing the circumstances leading to the attack and the events that preceded the dispute.
Article Summary: Vinay Gupta, 31, was allegedly assaulted at his home in Nihal Vihar, Delhi, on Friday. Police have detained four people in connection with the case. Gupta's father, Premchand, said the dispute was minor and that he initially believed the relatives had come to discuss the matter.

Article Title: Is Geno Smith already proving Aaron Glenn right about the Jets’ biggest gamble?

Geno Smith waited more than nine years to play another game in a New York Jets uniform. His return lasted one drive. Head coach Aaron Glenn saw enough from the 35-year-old quarterback to say the Jets got what they wanted from their new starter.Smith took the opening possession and moved the Jets 69 yards in 10 plays. The drive lasted nearly six minutes and ended with his 13-yard touchdown pass to tight end Jelani Woods.According to Jets.com contributor Jack Bell, Glenn praised Smith's command of the offense after the game.“Very, very efficient, he looked very comfortable,” Glenn said. “Exactly what we were looking for. But again, we still have some things we got to work on because our run game wasn't where it needs to be.”The numbers backed up the first part of Glenn's assessment. Smith went 7-for-7 and finished with a 144.9 passer rating. He completed passes to several targets and converted two third downs through the air. One went to tight end Mason Taylor for 10 yards. Another found Garrett Wilson for 10 yards and moved New York to Pittsburgh's 13-yard line.Smith threw the touchdown on the next play. His final stat line came from a tiny preseason sample, and Pittsburgh rested several starters. Still, Smith did what New York needed him to do. He moved the offense, handled pressure and finished the possession with seven points.That mattered after Smith missed the Jets' preseason opener because of a sore ankle. New York had indicated the injury was not considered serious, but Friday offered the first game look at its projected Week 1 starter.It also came with history attached.The Jets selected Smith in the second round of the 2013 NFL Draft. His previous start for New York came on Oct. 23, 2016, before a torn ACL ended his season. The franchise reacquired him from the Las Vegas Raiders in March 2026.Smith returned after throwing for 3,025 yards, 19 touchdowns and 17 interceptions in 15 games for Las Vegas last season.His first drive back in green looked considerably cleaner.Glenn's praise came with an immediate qualifier. He specifically pointed to New York's running game. The Jets had the result they wanted from Smith, but one efficient possession does not answer every offensive question before the regular season.Smith also refused to treat seven completions on seven attempts as a finished product.“There's always room for improvement, but we're always going to strive for perfection,” Smith said, according to Bell. “I don't really get too high or too low on anything. I think it's about the process, and I'm really focused on the process.”That approach fits where the Jets are right now.Smith is expected to start Week 1 against the Tennessee Titans, so New York did not need him playing deep into a preseason game. It needed evidence that he could operate the offense comfortably after the ankle issue.Friday provided exactly that. SNY's Lucas Hutcherson also noted Smith's work under pressure during the opening series. He stood in to complete throws and kept the drive moving on third down before finding Woods for the touchdown.The bigger test comes when the games count and defenses stop treating the night like an August evaluation.For now, Glenn has one drive of evidence. Smith completed every official pass he attempted, produced a touchdown and walked off the field healthy.The Jets close their preseason against the New York Giants on Friday, Aug. 28. After that, the evaluation changes.Smith's second stint in New York has officially reached the field. His first seven passes gave Glenn very little to complain about.

Article Title: Valkyrae’s AI controversy grows as streamer reveals the artist behind her disputed YouTube thumbnail
Article Text:
Valkyrae addresses AI allegations over YouTube thumbnail

Valkyrae defends thumbnail artist Anko

Rachell “Valkyrae” Hofstetter has addressed a growing debate over the artwork used for her YouTube livestreams after viewers accused her latest thumbnail of being AI-generated. The streamer defended her longtime thumbnail artist, Anko, while admitting she understands why some people reached that conclusion. Her comments also highlight a wider concern for digital artists as AI-generated content continues to reshape how audiences view online artwork.The controversy began after Anko, Valkyrae’s thumbnail artist, shared the creative process behind artwork for her Uncharted playthrough. The thumbnail initially received attention from viewers, but some quickly questioned whether artificial intelligence had been used to create it.That reaction eventually reached Valkyrae, who explained that Anko creates all of her YouTube livestream thumbnails and regularly shares his process online. She also pointed out the irony of the situation, saying that even those behind-the-scenes videos have not stopped people from making AI accusations.Valkyrae said:"Okay. We have to talk about this thumbnail debacle. I don't know what to do about this thumbnail debacle.So, as most of you know, every single one of my YouTube livestream thumbnails is made by the same artist. His name is Anko, and he makes all of them. He even posts on Twitter the art process of making them, but it still never beats the AI allegations. And the most recent thumbnail, he makes new thumbnails when I start a new game series, so, obviously, there is a new thumbnail for the Uncharted era. And people were saying, 'Oh, it's AI slop,' in the pre-chat."The streamer then offered a more nuanced response. Rather than dismissing viewers who suspected AI, she said she understood where their reaction came from. At the same time, she wanted to make clear that the artwork was not created using AI.Valkyrae added:"'Just ignore them.' Well, no. Okay? I don't blame people for thinking it's AI because AI is using people's art, like Anko's, to take over. But I would like to clear it up because there were a few people that were saying, 'Oh! When I saw the thumb, I also thought it was AI.' So now I am wondering how many people are out there that would watch the stream, but didn't because of the AI-looking thumbnail! But it's not AI."The discussion also became personal for Valkyrae because she said she felt bad for Anko. The thumbnail was later updated, with the artist adding his signature, giving viewers another indication of who created the work.Valkyrae explained that the situation made her think about the broader impact AI tools could have on working artists. For creators who depend on commissioned digital artwork, being mistaken for AI-generated work can create a difficult problem. The visual style that once helped an artist stand out can now cause audiences to question whether a human created it at all.She said:"I don't know, dude. I don't know what to do about it. I feel bad for him, though, because... and then, it, like, reminded me. I was like, 'Man, I just shouldn't do art thumbnails.' But then, the whole AI thing is doing what it does - making artists lose their jobs! Isn't that crazy?!"The controversy has now become more than a discussion about one YouTube thumbnail. Valkyrae’s response reflects a growing tension between AI-generated imagery and human-made digital art, particularly on social media where polished artwork can be judged within seconds.For Valkyrae, however, the message is straightforward: the Uncharted thumbnail was made by Anko, not AI. The debate instead shows how difficult it has become for artists to prove the human work behind their creations.
Article Summary: Valkyrae defends thumbnail artist Anko after viewers accuse him of being AI- generated. The streamer says she understands where people are coming from, but wants to make clear that the artwork was not created using AI. The debate shows how difficult it has become for artists to prove the human work behind their creations.

Article Title: "I'm grateful for every lesson": Gisele Bündchen’s candid Tom Brady divorce admission revealed the pain behind her new beginning
Article Text:

Gisele Bündchen opens up about Tom Brady divorce

Gisele Bündchen focuses on her children after divorce

Gisele Bündchen’s divorce from Tom Brady is no longer breaking news, but a deeply emotional 2024 interview still offers a revealing look at what the supermodel went through after their marriage ended. During a conversation with ABC News’ Robin Roberts, Bündchen struggled to hold back tears while reflecting on the end of a 13-year marriage, her children and the new chapter she was trying to build.The interview, released in March 2024 as part of “IMPACT x Nightline: Gisele Bündchen: Climbing the Mountain,” came more than a year after Bündchen and Brady finalized their divorce in October 2022.Their split ended a relationship that had lasted 16 years and a marriage that had lasted 13. By the time Bündchen sat down with Roberts, however, she was trying to understand the experience as part of a larger personal transition rather than simply an ending.Roberts reminded her that she had previously described the divorce as “the death of a dream.” The comment immediately struck an emotional chord.“Well, when you say ...” the model began, before pausing and getting teary. “Sorry, guys, I didn't know ... can I have a little moment?”After collecting herself, Bündchen spoke about accepting a future she had never expected to have.“It's definitely a time of, you know, a transition that had to take place, and it's not something that you — I don't think you wish for that, you know?” she said. “But I think sometimes in life things happen. I feel so blessed because, like, I wouldn't change anything in my life. I had incredible experiences. I learned so much. I have my children, which are the biggest blessings in my life.“And now I get to create — it's a new season, a new chapter in my life, and I get to learn new things, and I get to walk my path in a different way, you know?“And I'm grateful for all of it. I'm grateful for every lesson.”Her words showed that the divorce was not something she viewed in simple terms. There was pain, but there was also gratitude for the years she shared with Brady and the family they created.Bündchen and Brady share two children, Benjamin and Vivian. Brady also has a son, Jack, with actress Bridget Moynahan. For Bündchen, co-parenting meant accepting that the children would grow up moving between two different households and sets of rules.“There's easier days than others. But it's amazing that the kids — they're super smart children,” Bündchen said, laughing. “They know what they can get away with. So I think it's natural that it has different rules, and kids just adapt and they're going to try to do what they want. And I can only control what I do.”She also emphasized the value of her children having relationships with both parents.“It's amazing that they get to spend time with both parents because it's more enriching for their lives, two different worlds, and they get to learn from two different worlds.”Bündchen spoke warmly about Brady’s oldest son, Jack, whom she helped raise during her years with the former NFL star.“I raised him. I love him,” she said.Looking ahead, Bündchen said she wanted to live according to her own values rather than public expectations.“I'm very committed to living my truth more than ever, so I would say that's where my heart is now, where I am right now. I'm living my truth and I'm not apologizing for it,” she explained.The 2024 interview remains significant because it captured Bündchen at a vulnerable point in her life. She was not simply discussing a famous divorce. She was describing the difficult process of accepting change, protecting her children and finding an identity beyond a marriage that had once shaped so much of her public life.
Article Summary: Gisele Bündchen and Tom Brady finalized their divorce in October 2022. The supermodel struggled to hold back tears while reflecting on the end of a 13-year marriage. She said she wanted to live according to her own values rather than public expectations.

Article Title: Super Bowl LXI lands on Valentine’s Day for the first time in history creating an unusual football-versus-romance showdown
